trickyParts: The answer is taken from the end of a turn, which is weaker evidence than an authenticated op call, so four conditions narrow it and each is the claim as it stands at that end: the claim is in a round and has not answered it; its process runs a plugin that truly has no op (CannotAnswerUpdate, which reads the running process as well as the contract); the delivery this turn confirmed is an ask of that same round; and the turn ended on its own. The last is two checks, and the second was the deep review's High finding: m.interrupt lives in memory, so a daemon that restarts after its own Quiesce has no memory of the abort. askFirst is the durable half — NewMachine sets it for every restored StateWorking claim — and askTurnOver now leaves it for turnEnded to clear.
A refusal for either cut-turn check clears UpdateTaskedAt, so the round asks again at the next sweep rather than at pod_update_retask_hours. Without that a safe refusal would cost the round an hour.

The task's fallback tells the worker to end its last message with a WAITING line. A plugin below the update contract cannot reach the reminder's awaiting-update state, which only a successful ready_for_update sets, so without the WAITING line the phase reminder returns a continuation and the host turns the very turn whose end is the answer into one more turn. With it the stall moves to waiting at the first settle and the armed timer is 15 minutes rather than 5.

The pod round and the stale-plugin lane divide the claims between them, and the division is now one line: a claim in any round belongs to the round. Outside a round the lane is unchanged, and a Claude Code worker below the contract is still relaunched by nothing, because the relaunch would bring the same image's plugin back and walk the claim's launch budget down to failed.

LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN as the pod sets it names the `postgres` database, whose public schema the legion_test login cannot create in on PostgreSQL 18, so every daemon test that migrates into the DSN's own database fails `permission denied for schema public`. A database of this role's own (`createdb legion_infra484` as legion_test) fixes it; the DSN recorded in each proof above is that database.

The PR body's `Look at first` is the reviewer's line, and it named `supervise/table.go` `answeringRound`, a symbol round 4 deleted. Only that symbol was corrected, to `answerByTurnEnd`; the rest of the line and the whole `Not proven / risk` block are left for the reviewer.
openQuestions: A worker that answered by ending its turn has its answer taken back by any later turn (takeBackSignal), and the phase reminder starts one after 15 minutes with the WAITING line, 5 without. The round normally replaces the pod at the next sweep, a minute later, and a retraction re-asks at once, so the round converges; the bound is recorded here rather than removed, since removing it would mean exempting the reminder's own turn from takeBackSignal, which is the rule that stops a post-answer commit being lost.
discoveredComplexity: A defect of this pod rather than of the change, reported to the controller: internal/daemon's outbox-isolated tests drop their temporary database with `drop database … with (force)`, which needs the privilege to terminate the other sessions on it. The pod's legion_test role is NOSUPERUSER and holds no pg_signal_backend, and a `legion` superuser backend is live on that server (pg_stat_activity shows one), so those drops fail intermittently with `permission denied to terminate process` and the package cannot be run whole here. Each affected test passes when run alone. CI's run at this head is the evidence for the whole package.
